messages.author: b796ead63a4e495a
messages.subject: Covariate coefficient in removal model
parts:
Hello all,

I am trying to estimate the efficiancy of a fish monitoring system with the unmarked package and have problems interpreting covariate effects.

A three-pass-removal protocol was carried out on ten sites. On each of the ten sites an area of 1 ha was enclosed by a fish net and fish was captured by traps. This is the capture data, each row represents one site, the colums represent first, second and third pass and the cells contain counts of captured fish that was removed in each pass.

capture.obs <- matrix(
  c(7, 2, 0,
    10, 5, 2,
    10, 17, 7,
    5, 8, 2,
    5, 1, 1,
    4, 6, 2,
    10, 5, 1,
    9, 4, 1,
    3, 4, 4,
    6, 6, 4),
  ncol=3,byrow=T)


The fish was removed from the traps after 48 hours, 72 hours and 96 hours. In consequence, fishing effort was 48 hours in the first pass and 24 hours in the second and third pass. To account for effort I included the hours as detection covariates. This is my covariate matrix:

capture.covs <- list ("effort" = matrix(
  c(48, 24, 24,
    48, 24, 24,
    48, 24, 24,
    48, 24, 24,
    48, 24, 24,
    48, 24, 24,
    48, 24, 24,
    48, 24, 24,
    48, 24, 24,
    48, 24, 24),
  ncol=3,byrow=T))

Modeling code:

umf <- unmarkedFrameMPois(y = capture.obs,obsCov = capture.covs, type="removal")
fm <- multinomPois(~effort~1, capture.umf)
fm

Output:

> fm

Call:
multinomPois(formula = ~effort ~ 1, data = umf)

Abundance:
 Estimate    SE  z  P(>|z|)
     2.82 0.101 28 3.3e-172

Detection:
            Estimate     SE     z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)   1.0580 0.7463  1.42  0.1563
effort       -0.0295 0.0148 -2.00  0.0451

AIC: 152.7508



But when I try to conclude the detection probability of a single animal related to different amounts of fishing time, the results are strange. Backtransforming for 48 hours gives me an estimate of p=0.411:

> backTransform(linearComb(fm, coefficients = c(1,48), type = 'det'))
Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Detection estimate(s)

 Estimate     SE LinComb (Intercept) effort
    0.411 0.0464   -0.36           1     48

Transformation: logistic



Backtransforming for 24 hours should reduce the probability since we have lower fishing effort. But the estimate increases to p=0.586:


> backTransform(linearComb(fm, coefficients = c(1,24), type = 'det'))
Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Detection estimate(s)

 Estimate  SE LinComb (Intercept) effort
    0.586 0.1   0.349           1     24

Transformation: logistic


Can anyone explain to me what is wrong here? How do I interpret intercept and parameters of the detection model?

Thank you for any hints on this.
Jakob

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Covariate coefficient in removal model
parts:
Hi Jakob,

If the time intervals for each removal pass are variable, you could account for that using a custom "piFun" as is shown on the help page for "piFuns". You would just need to change the length of each time interval in this function:


# A user-defined piFun calculating removal probs when time intervals differ.
# Here 10-minute counts were divided into 2, 3, and 5 minute intervals.
# This function could be supplied to unmarkedFrameMPois along with the obsToY
# argument shown below.

instRemPiFun <- function(p) {
	M <- nrow(p)
	J <- ncol(p)
	pi <- matrix(NA, M, J)
	p[,1] <- pi[,1] <- 1 - (1 - p[,1])^2
	p[,2] <- 1 - (1 - p[,2])^3
	p[,3] <- 1 - (1 - p[,3])^5
	for(i in 2:J) {
		pi[,i] <- pi[, i - 1]/p[, i - 1] * (1 - p[, i - 1]) * p[, i]
		}
	return(pi)
	} 
	
instRemPiFun(pRem)

# Associated obsToY matrix required by unmarkedFrameMPois
o2y <- diag(3) # if y has 3 columns
o2y[upper.tri(o2y)] <- 1
o2y

When you run the model with this piFun, you will get an estimate of *hourly* capture probability.

Richard

messages.author: b796ead63a4e495a
messages.subject: Re: Covariate coefficient in removal model
parts:
Hi Richard,

thank you very much for your hint about the custom Pi function. I try to understand the function and the modeling procedure but I guess I am missing something very fundamental.

You mean I get an hourly estimate if I use 48, 24 and 24 as exponents inside the example function? This produces warnings, probably because the values get too small. 

In sqrt(diag(vcov(obj))) : NaNs produced

So I set it to 2, 1, 1 which from my understanding should account for 24hour windows (2 time units in pass 1; 1 time unit in pass 2 and pass 3). This leads to a detection estimation of backtransformed 0.02  which is far too small from what I know about the site. The population estimate goes up to 168 but is rather expected in a range below 20. By the way: I need an estimate for 48 hours.

Why does using fishing effort (measured by time) as a covariate not work?

Best
Jakob

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Covariate coefficient in removal model
parts:
hi Jakob,
from what I understand , your idea of using intervals of (2,1,1) should be correct. I would generally have expected very similar results between this approach and the previous approach you tried.
(and the result made sense there I think... there was a slightly negative effect of effort.... so the predictions reflect that). 

I believe it is this apparent negative effect of effort that may be throwing the results off in the 2nd analysis. The use of the piFun as suggested by Richard is a more strict assumption (independent, binomial detection) compared to the first approach of using effort as a covariate which allows for diminishing returns in catch per unit effort.  Still, the negative effect is weird and problematic... and I think this is what is throwing off the 2nd analysis.

regards
andy

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Covariate coefficient in removal model
parts:
I agree with everything that Andy said, but because we know a priori that capture probability can't go down with effort (when all else is equal), I wouldn't use the covariate approach. My guess is that there is some other important source of variation in capture probability that isn't being modeled. Perhaps there is a trap saturation issue? Or maybe there is high individual heterogeneity in capture probability. Those would be hard to deal with, but you might be able to soak up some of this variation by including occasion as covariate of p, while also allowing for unequal time intervals in the pi function.

messages.author: b796ead63a4e495a
messages.subject: Re: Covariate coefficient in removal model
parts:
Well, your explanations are reasonable. I didn't want to believe that the negative coefficient means negative impact of effort. Disbelieving was easy as I expected negative values out of the log transformation and I was not sure whether I understood the modeling formula at all.

Looking at the data and aggregating them to two time frames supports your explanation. The cumulative catch for the first 48 hours is 69 and for the next 48 hours (combining pass 2 and 3) is 82. The fish needs some time to learn how to get catched ;)

Richard, I am not sure about what you mean with occassion. You recommend to feed the pass number (1,2,3) as a covariate into the model?

Thank you all for thinking this through and helping me out.

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Covariate coefficient in removal model
parts:
I'm not sure if the parameters are identifiable when p is occasion-specific, but I played around with the data, and the model does fit better when you let p for the first occasion differ from p on occasions 2 and 3. Try this:

library(unmarked)

R <- nrow(capture.obs)
J <- ncol(capture.obs)

Occ <- matrix(c("First", "Second", "Third"), R, J, byrow=TRUE)
firstO <- matrix(c("First", "Not", "Not"), R, J, byrow=TRUE)

umf <- unmarkedFrameMPois(y=capture.obs,
                          obsCovs=list(firstO=firstO, Occ=Occ),
                          piFun="instRemPiFun", obsToY=o2y)

fm1 <- multinomPois(~1~1, umf)
summary(fm1)

fm2 <- multinomPois(~firstO~1, umf)
summary(fm2)

## fm3 <- multinomPois(~Occ~1, umf) ## Probably not identifiable
## summary(fm3)

predict(fm2, newdata=data.frame(firstO=c("First", "Not")), type="det", appendData=TRUE)

## 48 hr cap prob for first occasion
1-(1-0.23)^2

## 48 hr cap prob for other occasions
1-(1-0.58)^2

re <- ranef(fm2, K=50)
re

sum( predict(fm2, type="state")$Predicted) ## Expected abundance
sum(bup(re, stat="mode"))                  ## Realized abundance
sum(capture.obs)                           ## nCaptured

plot(re)

I played with using time (48,72,96) as covariate, but like including every occasion this is not stable.

What do you think, is it worth using a Bayesian approach for getting the point estimate / credibility interval? I guess the results will be quite similar since I don't have informed priors.

messages.author: b796ead63a4e495a
messages.subject: Re: Covariate coefficient in removal model
parts:
An addition to the covariate approach in combination with custom time intervals: Specifying a custom pi function is not neccessary when dummy coded first/other-occurence covariate is included. You get two coefficients, the first reflects 48h of first pass and the second 24h of other passes. They simply can be transformed to other time windows if neccessary (see Richard's code).

BTW: Bayesian approach brings up quite different results. I am still working on this.
